title: Keyhole, College Inn and the Bogalusa plantation club
summary: After the Keyhole failed as a higher-class club, the band played four years at the College Inn in Thibodaux and about seven at a Bogalusa plantation club, six nights a week.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Cabarets, honky-tonks and the Storyville nightlife scene

blocks.x: It's the beginning of, of what's big one? The keyhole. He closed the coconut roll down, see. You understand what I'm saying? And opened up the keyhole, see. We opened the keyhole, see. There. Well of course, he didn't do so good with that club because he had, what you would call, he didn't want them to go in there without the dress, collar and tie, and the man here to have a lady with them people, you know. Yeah, that's the place. Yeah, trying to make a higher class club out of. See, and then he had a couple of fights there and you shuffle out of there, you know, boys, a lot of girls would come there, girls would come in and they wouldn't let their fellas come in, you know, and all they wasn't dressed, you know. Right. Well then, he had to close that club down. We left there and went to the College Inn, stayed there four years. In Thibodeau, the College Inn, that's the swirl club. He played there. We left there, we played there four years. From the Adminos five years, we went, of course, we stayed four years. Now that's where the games, and I was here.
Then you played the plantation in Buggaloosa.
That's where the boys played there, that's right. Stayed there a long time. We stayed there about seven years. That's right. Cheater McNeese.
How many nights a week did you play?

We played every night at the plantation club, except Monday night. Six nights a week. Now that's where I made headlines at, in the Buggaloosa table. Oh yeah. I should have kept that table, I should have held that table, but I don't have it. I should have. When I got the slide, we were going back over to play, you know, and I was meeting the white people that had boys at the presentation, they all knew me, you know. They'd tell me about the media headlines, you know, in Buggaloosa. That's totally gone. I really went and grew up to play because I left there, when that club went down, we came to Avenue Lawn. We left there, we went to the corner room. We left there, went to the college inn.
You played six nights a week in all these places?

No, no, we played four nights at Avenue Lawn. Thursday, Friday, Saturday and Sunday. In Buggaloosa we played Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday, Friday, Saturday and Sunday. Of course, that's the first thing, you know, that's during the war, right off the war, see, 4-1-2, when Buggaloosa, one thing was a little good, we're good then, you know.
